papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving that adiabatic evolution with stoquastic frustration-free Hamiltonians is classically simulable and that stoquastic k-SAT is in MA and MA-hard for k = 6.

assertions.value: The paper proves (the main simulation theorem) that, when the adiabatic evolution conditions (A0)-(A3) are met, for any precision δ > 0 there is a classical probabilistic algorithm that generates x in {0, 1}^n from a distribution that approximates the ground-state distribution π(x) to within δ, with running time poly(n, δ−1).
quotes: Suppose the adiabatic evolution conditions (A0)-(A3) are met.
Then for any precision δ > 0 there exists a classical probabilistic algorithm that generates a random variable x ∈ {0, 1}n with a probability distribution
The running time of the algorithm is poly(n, δ−1).
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1.4 states the result with its conditions (A0)-(A3); Section 5 gives the proof.

assertions.value: The paper states (the proposition on frustration-free adiabatic evolution) that for a quantum circuit with L = poly(n) two-qubit gates and any precision δ > 0, one can construct a family of frustration-free Hamiltonians H(s), 0 ≤ s ≤ 1, on poly(n, δ−1) qubits satisfying conditions (A1), (A2) and (A3), such that the ground-state of H(1) approximates the circuit's output state with precision δ.

assertions.value: The authors state that Proposition 1.5 implies that simulating adiabatic evolution with frustration-free Hamiltonians is as hard as simulating a universal quantum computer, and that frustration-freeness alone cannot make adiabatic evolution efficiently simulatable on a classical computer.
